newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Americans jailed for Cyprus assault released.
newsitem.headline: Americans jailed for Cyprus assault released.

text.p: Three American professional basketball players and a U.S. marine have been pardoned after being jailed in Cyprus for up to 14 months for an attack on a policeman, officials said on Thursday.

Three of the prisoners were players in local basketball teams and the fourth was a marine at the U.S. embassy in capital Nicosia. They were released by a presidential pardon on July 4, just two weeks after their conviction by a Nicosia court.
Central prisons director George Anastassiades told the semi-official Cyprus News Agency (CNA) that the accused have since been deported.
Two of the Americans were jailed for 14 months, in June and the other two for 12 months for attacking an off-duty policeman in Nicosia when he apparently rebuked them for harassing his girlfriend.
All four pleaded guilty to causing the policeman actual bodily harm, a charge that carries a maximum sentence of up to seven years in jail.
Private Cypriot television station Sigma reported that the police officer, a member of the elite anti-terrorist unit, was compensated by the accused for the attack with 5000 pounds ($9625).
